newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm vs dlr amid increased inflows.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm vs dlr amid increased inflows.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling firmed marginally against the dollar on Wednesday boosted by large dollar inflows amid subdued demand, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.92 against the dollar from 54.93 on Tuesday, while against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 87.47 from 87.23.
Dealers attributed the excess supply of dollars to players unwinding long dollar positions accumulated over a number of days.
"There were a lot of inflows too from foreign investors and the traditional tea auction sales," another dealer said.

They added that passive intervention by the central bank only helped the shilling retrace it's steps back to the thin band traded over the last three weeks, a stabilising effect,but overall did not stop the sentiment for a stronger shilling.
Some dealers said if it wasn't for dollar buying initiative by the central bank, the shilling would definitely be stronger -- around the 54.60/70 region, as demand was relatively low.
A stable shilling sustained by central bank and attractive interest rate differentials relative to other countries have increased the number of foreign investors looking to invest in treasury bills.
The money market tightened as players positioned themselves to make out tax payments, due on Thursday.
Overnight rates were quoted at between 15-20 percent compared to 9-15 percent on Tuesday.
